criteria.name: B33-1
criteria.text: Every coefficient of the Thirteenth Schedule is exactly two-thirds of the corresponding coefficient of the Twelfth, over all seven bands and four age columns, slopes and intercepts alike.

criteria.name: B33-2
criteria.text: The Fourteenth Schedule is cell for cell identical to the Twelfth; only the variable it is read against differs (total monthly sum against average monthly income).

criteria.detail: 5 written classes carrying 6 clause vectors, 0 colliding pairs
criteria.name: B33-3
criteria.text: No two of the classes the instrument writes receive an identical clause vector on all five dimensions. A collision would put the read partition strictly coarser than the written one.

criteria.name: B33-4
criteria.text: Every page of the instrument was opened, and the coverage table names what each batch carried, including batches that carried nothing bearing on the criteria.

criteria.detail: 1 of 5 written classes carry more than one vector: 8AB eligible Group A worker
criteria.name: B33-5
criteria.text: Where the read partition is strictly finer than the written one, the extra line is drawn by the instrument itself and can be named. Every class carrying more than one clause vector has its dividing provisions listed; a split with no provision behind it would put the read partition finer than the written one and fail the arm.

criteria.detail: 2 period pairing(s); dimensions differing per pairing [4, 4]
criteria.name: B33-26
criteria.opposite_prediction: the counting law puts the number of distinct clause values at the number of classes the programme writes, so this frame predicts the two differ where the rival predicts they coincide. The cell admits both outcomes (discipline 11e, sixth clause).
criteria.polarity: registered as the rival's prediction failing, so passing means the rival is wrong (discipline 11e, first clause, second part)
criteria.rival_entailment: 8AB and 8AC stand at one position: their eligibility sentences are the same word for word but for the group name, and what separates the groups is the member's date of birth plus an option that runs one way and cannot be withdrawn, neither of which is a position variable. Terms generated by one scalar at one position must therefore coincide across the two classes, on every dimension and in every period. One differing dimension refutes it.
criteria.rival_premise: a position carries a scalar and every term at that position is generated by it, so the object has one index and no class index
criteria.text: On the one pair that stands at one position, 8AB and 8AC, the rival's scalar generates one set of terms, so the two classes must receive identical clause vectors in every period pairing. The criterion counts the dimensions on which they differ and passes when every pairing differs on at least one.

chain: S 156/2025 reg 3(b): the two terms have the meanings given by paragraph 1(1) of the Fourth Schedule to the Act
Fourth Schedule para 1(1): Group A is a platform worker to whom Part 3 applies as set out in para 5; Group B, Part 4 as set out in para 8
group_partition.group_a: para 5: born on or after 1 January 1995; or born before and opting to be a Group A worker under para 4(1)
group_partition.group_b: para 8: born before 1 January 2026, subject to paras 5, 6 and 7
group_partition.not_reducible_to_age: both schedules are banded by age, so a reading that the terms are a function of age has to be answered.  The one-way option answers it: a worker born before 1995 who has exercised it is Group A while a worker of the same age in the same month who has not is Group B.  The class index is a label the Board records, not a function of any position variable.
group_partition.option_one_way: para 4(3): an option under sub-paragraph (1) cannot be withdrawn.  The option runs from B to A only, and a worker born on or after 1 January 1995 has no route to Group B at all.
group_partition.same_position: the eligibility sentences of 8AB and 8AC are the same word for word but for the group name: being a Group X worker, worked as a platform worker (and not also as an employee) in the relevant month.  What the member did is identical; the terms are not.

8AB eligible Group A worker: reg 13B(1)(b)(ii): the cash proportion moves from one-tenth to two-fifths at applicable year 2029
reg 13C(2)(b): the benefit table moves from the Thirteenth to the Twelfth Schedule at applicable year 2029
